 ORDER
This petition has been filed to quash the FIR registered in Crime No.24 of 2022 on the file of the first respondent police.

2. On the complaint lodged by the second respondent, the first respondent has registered an FIR as against the petitioner in Cr.No.24 of 2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 376 and 506(1) of IPC, 1860, on the allegations that the second respondent is a Muslim and the first petitioner is a Hindu.
The first petitioner and the second respondent were initially friends and thereafter they have entered into a consensual relationship.
When the family members of the first petitioner came to know about their relationship, they have objected the same.
Even then, the first petitioner has assured the second respondent that he would marry her.

Believing the said words,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:52 pm ) the second respondent had awaited for her marriage with the first petitioner.
While being so, on 30.07.2022, the second respondent came to know that the first respondent got engaged with another lady for their marriage.
When the second respondent has attempted to contact him, the first petitioner has denied the said allegation and he has again given assurance that he will marry the second respondent.
Hence, the complaint.
3. Though notice was served on the second respondent and her name is also printed in the cause-list, there is no representation before this Court either in person or through Counsel.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that originally the second respondent has filed a complaint before the first respondent.

After conducting preliminary enquiry,
the first respondent has closed the said complaint on the ground that the second respondent wanted to withdraw the said complaint and not to proceed as against the first petitioner.

5. The learned counsel further submits that once again, the second respondent has filed a petition by way of a private complaint https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:52 pm ) forwarded the same under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C through the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Additional Mahila Court, Erode in Crl.MP.No.751 of 2022.
The learned Magistrate vide order dated 23.02.2022, directed the first respondent to conduct enquiry and if any cognizable offence is made out, register an FIR and report before the Court.

6. The learned counsel further submits that as directed by the learned Magistrate of Additional Mahila Court, Erode, the first respondent has conducted a detailed enquiry and filed a report before the learned Magistrate on the same day.

There is no primafacie material to register the FIR as R.Nandhakumar vs State Of Tamilnadu on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33726380/
2 against the petitioner.
That apart, the second respondent got married to another person and is living separately.
The said report was accepted by the learned Magistrate and closed.

However, once again fresh complaint was lodged by the second respondent before the first respondent and the first respondent has mechanically registered the FIR without considering the earlier two complaints and closure report.
Infact, the report submitted by the first respondent was accepted by the learned Magistrate the petition https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:52 pm )
in Crl.MP.N.751 of 2022 was closed.

7. A perusal of records revealed that once, the learned Magistrate has accepted the report submitted by the first respondent, the first respondent should not have registered the FIR that too after getting permission from the Court.
8. Further, a perusal of the closure report dated 19.04.2022 revealed that on the complaint lodged by the second respondent, does not provide any material information to act on the said proceedings.

The second respondent has not mentioned the place, date and time of occurrence in the complaint nor produced medical statement or records to corroborate the allegations levelled against the petitioner.
Therefore, the complaint lodged against the second respondent does not disclose primafacie materials constituting any offence as against the petitioner.
9. That apart, even according to the second respondent, the petitioner never gave false promise to marry the second respondent and had consensual intercourse with her.
Further, the second r e s p o n d e n t i s a l s o a g e d a b o u t 3 1 y e a r s .
T h e r e f o r e , s h e k n o w s a b o u t https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:52 pm ) the consequence of a physical relationship.

Therefore, it will not attract the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
10.
In so far as other offences are concerned, the second and third petitioner never gave any promise to marry the second respondent to the first petitioner.
Thereafter there was no threatening caused by the petitioners to the second respondent.

Therefore, the offence under Sections 471 and 506(i)
are not attractsed as per the allegations levelled against the petitioners.
Therefore, on the face of the FIR it does not constitute any offence.
In such case no question of appreciating evidence would arise.
In such case, it could be legitimate for this court to hold that it would be manifestly unjust to allow the process of the crime number to be issued against the petitioner.

11. It is also relevant to extract the judgement reported in (1992) SCC Crl. 426 in the case of Bajanlal v. State of Haryana, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has listed out the following category of case in which the criminal proceedings can be quashed using the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court under https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:52 pm )
Section 482 Cr.P.C.:
"102..........
...................

3 7.

Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceedings is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wrecking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
12. In view of the above, FIR cannot be sustained and is liable to be quashed, since the second respondent got married to another person and is living separately.
Therefore, the second respondent also has no interest to pursue the FIR.
That apart, the FIR is of the year 2022 and there has been no progress after that.
13. Mere by keeping the FIR pending for the past 3 years would not serve any purpose.

Therefore,
this Court is inclined to quash the FIR to meet the ends of justice.
Accordingly, the FIR registered in Crime No.24 of 2022 on the file of the first respondent police is hereby quashed.
14. In the result, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
